newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London mixed ahead of triple-witch.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London mixed ahead of triple-witch.

text.p: U.S. shares in London were mixed in thin, cautious trade as many investors stayed on the sidelines ahead of Friday's "triple-witching" expiration of U.S. stock index futures and options contracts, dealers said.
"We've seen a little business but most people are holding back until they see the impact of the triple-witching," one market maker said.
"It's hard to predict how the Dow will react. We just don't know if people squared positions yesterday or if there is more to come. It's going to be a crazy day."

The Dow industrials soared 126.87 points on Thursday, with some analysts citing the approaching expiration of December index futures and options contracts as well as individual stock options as a primary force in the dramatic rise.
General Electric, which rose $3-3/4 on Thursday after announcing a 2-for-1 stock split and increased share repurchase programme, was up $1/4 from the New York close at $103.
Barrick Gold was up $1/4 at $30-1/4, helped by positive comment about the company's stake in the huge Busang gold find in Indonesia.
High-technology shares were mixed with Texas Instruments down $1/8 at $64 while IBM rose $1/8 at $158-1/4.

Automotives were weaker following news that General Motors had reduced its Q4 earnings estimates. Ford was down $1/4 at $31-3/8 while Chrysler and GM bothed eased $1/8 at $33 and $54-3/8 respectively.
The March S&P 500 futures contract on the Globex after-hours trading system, was up 1.25 points at 754.75 by 1055 GMT while the March T-bond added 6/32 at 113-11/32.
